intentions.title: Enforce Workspace as the hard multi-tenant boundary with a single total authorization chokepoint
intentions.evidence: Barkpark.Tenancy.Auth.authorize/3 is documented as THE entry point router/controllers call; it is total (unknown action/non-member/unrecognised principal → {:error, :forbidden} rather than raising); cross-tenant isolation guaranteed by membership lookup keyed on (principal_id, workspace_id, principal_type) in membership/2 clauses in auth.ex.

intentions.title: Unify API-token and logged-in-user principals under one membership+role authorization model
intentions.evidence: Membership.principal_type ("api_token"|"user") discriminates two principal kinds; Auth.authorize/3 has separate clauses for %ApiToken{} (permissions[] array) and %User{} (membership role), both funneled through the same membership lookup and action vocabulary (:read/:write/:admin) in auth.ex.

intentions.title: Prevent cross-tenant privilege escalation: a token's global permissions never imply admin rights in a workspace it didn't create
intentions.evidence: auth.ex @default_role "member" and role_for_permissions/1 docstring explicitly cite bug fixes barkpark-23yi/barkpark-fsko: a token ADDED to a workspace defaults to member regardless of global perms; role_for_permissions is scoped ONLY to a token's own home-workspace mint binding; workspace_admin?/2 checks the per-membership role, not global perms.

intentions.title: Support data-driven custom RBAC roles per workspace while keeping built-in roles (owner/admin/member) tamper-proof
intentions.evidence: role.ex: nil workspace_id = global built-in, set workspace_id = custom role scoped to workspace; role_permission.ex stores granted actions; auth.ex granted_actions/2 ALWAYS resolves built-in names from the compiled @builtin_role_actions map (ignoring any DB row of the same name) so a tenant can't redefine 'admin' to escalate, while custom roles resolve purely from DB rows; valid_role_names/1 in Auth widens accepted membership roles per-workspace.

intentions.title: Guarantee authorization never silently locks out built-in roles even on an unseeded or corrupted database
intentions.evidence: auth.ex @builtin_role_actions comment: 'compiled-in action sets ... the fail-safe when no DB role_permissions row exists ... because enforcement falls back to this map, a fresh/unseeded DB (or a lost row) can NEVER silently lock out a built-in role'.

intentions.title: Model a strict tenancy hierarchy — Organization > Workspace > Project > Dataset — as an additive, non-breaking layering
intentions.evidence: organization.ex: thin tier ABOVE Workspace, nullable organization_id, 'no authorization path reads it yet', anchor for future SSO/SCIM; project.ex: Project lives under exactly one Workspace, slug unique within workspace; dataset.ex ('Wave-2'): Dataset lives under exactly one Project, dataset string stays authoritative while dataset_id rides alongside additively until later steps flip over.

intentions.title: Route safety: reserve slug namespaces so workspace/project slugs can never collide with system routes
intentions.evidence: workspace.ex and project.ex both define @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api _plugins studio login media v1 w p) and validate_exclusion(:slug, @reserved_slugs) in their changesets.

intentions.title: Guarantee complete, hook-respecting workspace deletion with no orphaned blobs, CDN cache, or skipped plugin hooks
intentions.evidence: workspace.ex @moduledoc mandates using Tenancy.delete_workspace/1, never raw Repo.delete/1: walks media_files firing Media.delete_file/1 (blob + CDN purge + :after_media_delete hook) and documents firing Content.delete_document/1 (:before_delete/:after_delete hooks) before the CASCADE delete; test/barkpark/tenancy_delete_workspace_test.exs proves the raw-delete leak as a deliberate control case.

intentions.title: Lay groundwork for enterprise SSO/SCIM and org-wide policy enforcement (e.g. mandatory MFA) via the Organization tier
intentions.evidence: organization.ex require_mfa field with era-w2-org-require-mfa comment: 'every user who is a member (via any of this org's workspaces) must have an MFA factor enrolled ... Governing rule across orgs: ANY-org-requires → enforce'; described as opt-in/additive today, anchor for future SSO/SCIM connections.
